title: openalex_W2947015376
universal_lens: The structural unification of motion planning and optimal control relies on mapping a non-convex trajectory optimization problem onto a constrained variational calculus framework. This primitive formalizes the transition from abstract high-level commands to continuous state-space trajectories, governed by differential constraints and performance metrics. Nonlinear optimization frameworks unify constrained minimization through merit functions and iterative progress measures across GSI Bayesian inference and GSE state-transition dynamics.
gsi_mapping: In GSI, this maps to Bayesian inference over latent player trajectories. The optimal control formulation provides the likelihood function for physical movement, while conformal prediction bounds quantify the epistemic uncertainty in reconstructing an athlete's intended path given noisy tracking data and environmental constraints. GSI employs merit function-based convergence criteria to map probabilistic belief updates in high-dimensional parameter spaces via conformal predictive distributions over nonlinear program solutions.
gse_mapping: For GSE, this primitive drives situational reasoning by defining valid state-transitions within a game engine. It calculates the minimum energy or time required for an agent to reach a target zone, dynamically adjusting to real-time obstacles and actuator limitations inherent in biomechanical models. GSE leverages trust-region and line-search mechanisms to model dynamic state transitions in motion planning and optimal control, ensuring iterative progress toward terminal goals under constraint violations.

primitives.name: Optimal Control Motion Planner
primitives.verbatim_quote: From a control perspective, the resulting problem is an instance of an optimal control problem.
primitives.latex: \min_{x,u} \int_{t_0}^{t_f} L(x(t), u(t)) dt \quad \text{s.t.} \quad \dot{x}(t) = f(x(t), u(t)), \ x(t_0)=x_0
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: x: State vector (meters, radians); u: Control input (Newtons, dimensionless); L: Lagrangian cost function (Joules/second); t: Time (seconds); f: Dynamics function (m/s, rad/s)
primitives.assumptions: System dynamics are differentiable; state and control spaces are continuous; boundary conditions are strictly defined.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when the Hessian of the Lagrangian loses positive definiteness, leading to local minima traps in highly non-convex obstacle-rich environments.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSE's tactical pathfinding where minimizing L corresponds to maximizing expected points per possession under defensive pressure.
layer2.telemetry: Convergence rate of sequential convex programming algorithms and deviation from global optimum.

The empirical evaluation demonstrates that using complete vehicle dynamics (Pdyn) yields superior performance compared to kinematic (Pkin) or geometric (Pgeo) approximations, highlighting the importance of incorporating system dynamics.
